summary: Shadow traffic enablement triggered metrics cardinality alerts (telemetry/Prometheus) for Dedicated tenant
content:
Issue Summary
- After enabling Shadow Traffic (beta) for Aurora Devtools’ Dedicated tenant, our metrics backend began firing high-cardinality alerts and write rejections.
- Primary impact was internal: reduced observability fidelity and increased risk to telemetry stability. Customer-facing API serving remained healthy.

Customer Report (via CSM escalation)
- Aurora enabled shadow experiments on their highest-QPS route to compare control vs candidate variant.
- Within ~20 minutes, their Console “Quality deltas” dashboards showed gaps and delayed updates.
- They also reported that some internal dashboards they rely on (latency breakdown panels) became “partial / missing series.”

Impact
- Telemetry ingestion: elevated series churn and increased dropped samples.
- Metrics backend (Mimir/Prometheus) triggered cardinality alarms; some write paths began rate limiting.
- Console quality panels were missing segments due to aggregation dropping high-cardinality dimensions.

Environment
- Dedicated tenant: Aurora Devtools
- Region: us-east
- Feature: Shadow traffic telemetry events v1 + quality delta dashboards

Timeline (UTC)
- 2026-02-12 16:05: Pager triggered for cardinality threshold breach on shadow telemetry metric families.
- 2026-02-12 16:12: Support engaged Observability + Telemetry (Caleb Johnson, Nadia Rahman).
- 2026-02-12 16:35: Confirmed correlation with new shadow traffic dimension set (per-route + per-target + request fingerprint bucket).
- 2026-02-12 17:10: Mitigation applied: reduced emitted dimensions via allowlist override for tenant; forced bucketing for route identifiers.
- 2026-02-13: Patch prepared to change defaults for all beta tenants (drop unsafe labels, enforce bucketing, cap series).
- 2026-02-14: Verified stability and closed ticket after 24h clean metrics.

Signals / Alerts
- Alert: "mimir_ingester_series_limit_near" (multiple ingesters)
- Alert: "prom_remote_write_samples_dropped" increased
- Internal dashboard: Shadow quality delta panels: missing data for segment breakdowns

Investigation Notes
Findings
1) The shadow telemetry events were being translated into multiple metric families with a label set that included at least one effectively-unbounded dimension under Aurora’s traffic:
   - route_id (string, high variety due to per-team routing keys)
   - shadow_target_id (fine)
   - model_id (fine)
   - experiment_id (fine)
   - prompt_id / request_fingerprint (NOT fine at Dedicated QPS; effectively unique per request)

2) Aurora’s workload had high variance in request metadata headers. Even though we intended to strip most headers, a “shadow_metadata_hash” label was being propagated in one metric path.

3) Existing cardinality guardrails in the Shadow Traffic design were partially implemented but not enabled by default for this tenant (beta config drift). The ADR guidance (adr-shadow-metrics-data-model-and-cardinality) states request-unique identifiers must never become metric labels; they must live in logs/traces with sampling.

Reproduction
- Enable shadow policy on a high-QPS route (>= 200 RPS) with segment breakdown enabled in Console.
- If request_fingerprint/prompt_id is emitted as a label, series count grows ~linearly with traffic.

Immediate Mitigation (2026-02-12)
- Applied tenant-level allowlist for shadow metrics dimensions:
  - Dropped: prompt_id, request_fingerprint, shadow_metadata_hash
  - Forced bucketing: route_id -> route_bucket (stable 128-bucket hash)
  - Limited: segment_key -> {"none", "country_group", "sdk_family"} (pre-approved set)
- Disabled per-request example sampling export for Aurora until patch landed (kept async scoring running; only metrics emission was reduced).
- Confirmed “fail-open” serving path unaffected; no additional routing overhead observed.

Customer Communication
- 2026-02-12: Informed Aurora that the issue is metrics-only (no serving impact), and we’re applying safe default dimensions immediately.
- Shared guidance: run shadow at 1–2% sampling while we deploy defaults; avoid enabling per-request segment breakdowns on day 1.

Resolution
Root cause
- Shadow traffic metrics pipeline emitted one or more request-unique identifiers as labels for aggregation, causing a cardinality explosion in the metrics backend when enabled on high-volume routes.

Fix / Changes Implemented
- Reduced default dimensions for all shadow-traffic quality metrics:
  - Removed request-unique labels from metric paths (request_fingerprint/prompt_id/metadata hash).
  - Enforced a strict label allowlist, matching the ADR and the Quality Metrics Observability Standard.
  - Added hard caps + drop counters when a new label key/value is not on the allowlist.
- Updated dashboard queries to use safe breakdowns only (route_group, model_id, shadow_target_id, rubric_version).
- Added runbook note + Console warning: segment breakdowns are limited to approved low-cardinality dimensions; anything else is sampled and only available via example logs.

Verification
- 2026-02-13 to 2026-02-14: No recurrence of cardinality alerts; dropped samples returned to baseline.
- Aurora Console quality deltas panels populated normally (with reduced breakdown options).

Follow-ups / Action Items
- ENG-5410: Implement platform-wide cardinality guardrails for shadow metrics (hard enforcement + tests for "no request-unique labels").
- Telemetry: Add canary check in pipeline deploy to measure series growth for new metric families.
- Docs: Update Shadow Traffic quickstart to include “safe dimensions” table + recommended sampling defaults for high-QPS Dedicated tenants.

Support Notes
- If customer requests per-request drilldown: route them to sampled examples view (logs) instead of metric labels.
- If customer needs custom segmentation: requires design review; do not add new label keys without observability approval.

Participants
- Support/Obs: Allison Grant (reporter), Caleb Johnson (assignee)
- Telemetry: Nadia Rahman
- Platform/Policy: Jordan Lee (consulted)
- Customer: Aurora Devtools (Dedicated)
